issue_context.title: `#with` doesn't accept three or more sub-queries
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

`#with` method doesn't accept three or more sub-queries.

```ruby
# 2 sub-queries are OK
irb> User.with(foo: [User.select(:id), User.select(:id)]).to_sql
=> "WITH `foo` AS ( SELECT `users`.`id` FROM `users` UNION ALL SELECT `users`.`id` FROM `users` ) SELECT `users`.* FROM `users`"

# 3 sub-queries raise an error
irb> User.with(foo: [User.select(:id), User.select(:id), User.select(:id)]).to_sql
in `<main>': undefined method `union' for an instance of Arel::Nodes::UnionAll (NoMethodError)

        when Array then value.map { |q| build_with_expression_from_value(q) }.reduce { |result, value| result.union(:all, value) }
                                                                                                             ^^^^^^
```

### Expected behavior

Build a query that combined all sub-queries with `UNION ALL`

### Actual behavior

An error occurs

> undefined method `union' for an instance of Arel::Nodes::UnionAll (NoMethodError)

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 7.2.1

**Ruby version**: 3.3.0
comments: Was able to reproduce and found the root cause, going to open a PR.

review_comments:
Need this for sqlite to make sure that queries used in `UNION` are not wrapped by parenthesis, because it is an invalid syntax.

`select .. union select ..` is good, but `(select ..) union (select ..)` is invalid 🤦
